That reality is what pushed him onto the path that seemed the most accessible. “I don’t come from a poor family, but I still took the easiest path for me at the time,” he says, vaguely alluding to the illegal activities that led him to where he is. “When you’re young and you see people around you who are fly, who dress well, you’re amazed by that. Rester dans le même cycle ou se reprendr: Stay in the same cycle or take charge of his life again? At that point in his life, that was the question Racci was asking himself. Worn down, he chose to bet on himself and go with the second option. “I started working out, reading, eating properly. I changed my whole way of life. And by changing my way of life, the people I hung around with changed too,” he says.

Once you’re out, the risk of relapse is high.
« J’ai commencé à boxer. Chaque jour, po: “I started boxing. Every day, to pass the time, I went to train at the gym. Boxing allowed him to get back in shape physically, but also emotionally and psychologically.

« Mon esprit d’entrepreneur me vient de: “My entrepreneurial spirit comes from the street, and my discipline comes from boxing,” he sums up.

As a guy from the east end of the island himself, he understands better than anyone the issues and challenges young people face.
« Je savais quel était le besoin du quar: “I knew what the neighbourhood needed.
